<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Important information about access to shareholder reports</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Beginning on January 1, 2021, as permitted by regulations
adopted by the Securities and Exchange Commission, paper copies of your fund&rsquo;s annual and semiannual shareholder reports
will no longer be sent to you by mail, unless you specifically request them. Instead, you will be notified by mail each time a
report is posted on the website and will be provided with a link to access the report.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">If you have already elected to receive shareholder reports
electronically, you will not be affected by this change and do not need to take any action. You may elect to receive shareholder
reports and other communications from the fund electronically by contacting your financial intermediary (such as a broker-dealer
or bank) or, if you invest directly with the fund, by calling Vanguard at one of the phone numbers on the back cover of this report
or by logging on to vanguard.com.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">You may elect to receive paper copies of all future
shareholder reports free of charge. If you invest through a financial intermediary, you can contact the intermediary to
request that you continue to receive paper copies. If you invest directly with the fund, you can call Vanguard at one of the
phone numbers on the back cover of this report or log on to vanguard.com. Your election to receive paper copies will apply to
all the funds you hold through an intermediary or directly with Vanguard.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>A Note From Our CEO</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><IMG SRC="tv514089-500indeximg02.jpg" ALT=""></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Tim Buckley</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Chairman and Chief Executive Officer</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Dear Shareholder,</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Over the years, I&rsquo;ve found that prudent investors exhibit
a common trait: discipline. No matter how the markets move or what new investing fad hits the headlines, those who stay focused
on their goals and tune out the noise are set up for long-term success.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">The prime gateway to investing is saving, and you don&rsquo;t
usually become a saver without a healthy dose of discipline. Savers make the decision to sock away part of their income, which
means spending less and delaying gratification, no matter how difficult that may be.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Of course, disciplined investing extends beyond diligent
saving. The financial markets, in the short term especially, are unpredictable; I have yet to meet the investor who can time them
perfectly. It takes discipline to resist the urge to go all-in when markets are frothy or to retreat when things look bleak.&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Staying put with your investments is one strategy for handling
volatility. Another, rebalancing, requires even more discipline because it means steering your money away from strong performers
and toward poorer performers.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Patience&mdash;a form of discipline&mdash;is also the friend
of long-term investors. Higher returns are the potential reward for weathering the market&rsquo;s turbulence and uncertainty.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">It&rsquo;s important to be prepared for that turbulence, whenever
it appears. Don&rsquo;t panic. Don&rsquo;t chase returns or look for answers outside the asset classes you trust. And be sure to
rebalance periodically, even when there&rsquo;s turmoil.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Whether you&rsquo;re a master of self-control, get a boost
from technology, or work with a professional advisor, know that discipline is necessary to get the most out of your investment
portfolio. And know that Vanguard is with you for the entire ride.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Thank you for your continued loyalty.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Sincerely,</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><IMG SRC="tv514089-500indeximg03.jpg" ALT="">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Mortimer J. Buckley</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Chairman and Chief Executive Officer</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">January 17, 2019</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>Your Fund&rsquo;s Performance
at a Glance</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the 12 months ended December 31, 2018, Vanguard 500 Index Fund returned &ndash;4.52% for Investor Shares and &ndash;4.43% for Admiral
Shares. The fund, which provides exposure to the stocks of the largest U.S. companies, closely tracked its target index, the Standard
&amp; Poor&rsquo;s 500 Index, which returned &ndash;4.38%. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
broad U.S. stock market returned about &ndash;5%, its first negative calendar-year result since 2008. Growth stocks outperformed
value; large-capitalization stocks bested small- and mid-caps. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Among
sectors, financials and industrials were the biggest detractors. Health care and information technology contributed most. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the ten years ended December 31, 2018, the 500 Index Fund posted an average annual return of about 13%, in line with its target
index. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
November, Vanguard lowered the investment minimum for your fund&rsquo;s Admiral Shares from $10,000 to $3,000. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>About Your Fund&rsquo;s
Expenses</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which
include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating
expenses, which are deducted from a fund&rsquo;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">A fund&rsquo;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its
average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing
costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based
on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">The accompanying table illustrates your fund&rsquo;s costs
in two ways:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>Based
on actual fund return</B>. This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &ldquo;Ending
Account Value&rdquo; shown is derived from the fund&lsquo;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would
have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount
you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for
example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the
heading &ldquo;Expenses Paid During Period.&rdquo;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT> <FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>Based
on hypothetical 5% yearly return</B>. This section is intended to help you compare your fund&lsquo;s costs with those of other
mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In
this case&mdash;because the return used is not the fund&rsquo;s actual return&mdash;the results do not apply to your investment.
The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate
expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&rsquo;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical
examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight
and help you compare <I>ongoing</I> costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling
securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus.
If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &ldquo;sales load.&rdquo;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during
the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases
or redemptions.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">You can find more information about the fund&rsquo;s expenses,
including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses
and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&rsquo;s current prospectus.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"></P>

&ldquo;Expenses Paid&rdquo; are equal to the annualized expense ratio multiplied by the average account value over the period,

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>500 Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>Notes to Financial Statements</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Vanguard 500 Index Fund is registered under the Investment
Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares,
ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Select Shares. Each of the share classes has different eligibility and minimum purchase
requirements, and is designed for different types of investors. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased
and sold through a broker.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">On November 19, 2018, the fund announced changes to the availability
and minimum investment criteria of the Investor and Admiral share classes. It is anticipated that all of the outstanding Investor
Shares will be automatically converted to Admiral Shares beginning in April 2019, with the exception of those held by Vanguard
funds and certain other institutional investors.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>A</B>. The following significant accounting policies conform
to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing
its financial statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close
of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued
at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which
market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&rsquo;s
pricing time but after the close of the securities&rsquo; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees
to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&rsquo;s net asset value. Temporary
cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors
as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts
to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing
transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in
response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance
for liquidity. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market
values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty
risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further
mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers
and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin
requirements to secure the fund&rsquo;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the
market value of each contract. Any assets pledged as initial margin for open contracts are noted in the Statement of Net Assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement
prices. The notional amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the
contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized
appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font: normal 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><TD STYLE="width: 33%">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->22<!-- Field: /Sequence --></TD><TD STYLE="width: 33%">&nbsp;</TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>500 Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">During the year ended December 31, 2018, the fund&rsquo;s
average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the
average of the notional amounts at each quarter-end during the period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify
as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&rsquo;s tax positions
taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2015&ndash;2018), and has concluded that no provision for federal income
tax is required in the fund&rsquo;s financial statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded
on the ex-dividend date. Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital
gains for financial reporting purposes.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund
lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time, and
are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily
market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When
this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled before the opening of the market on the next business day. The fund further
mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties,
monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master
securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&rsquo;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may
terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed
to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the event
of a default, the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received
in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during
the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested
cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan. During the term of the loan, the fund is entitled to all distributions
made on or in respect of the loaned securities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed
by The Vanguard Group (&ldquo;Vanguard&rdquo;) participate in a $3.1 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate
of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if
any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&rsquo;s
regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment
fee of 0.10% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&rsquo;s
board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&rsquo;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings
under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon the higher of the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate, federal funds
effective rate, or overnight bank funding rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2018,
or at any time during the period then ended.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">7. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date.
Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts
on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>500 Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions
are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment
securities are those of the specific securities sold.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings,
except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included
in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each
class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses
on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>B</B>. In accordance with the terms of a Funds&rsquo;
Service Agreement (the &ldquo;FSA&rdquo;) between Vanguard and the fund, Vanguard furnishes to the fund investment advisory, corporate
management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services at Vanguard&rsquo;s cost of operations (as defined by the FSA).
These costs of operations are allocated to the fund based on methods and guidelines approved by the board of trustees. Vanguard
does not require reimbursement in the current period for certain costs of operations (such as deferred compensation/benefits and
risk/insurance costs); the fund&rsquo;s liability for these costs of operations is included in Payables to Vanguard on the Statement
of Net Assets. All other costs of operations payable to Vanguard are generally settled twice a month.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Upon the request of Vanguard, the fund may invest up to 0.40%
of its net assets as capital in Vanguard. At December 31, 2018, the fund had contributed to Vanguard capital in the amount of $23,100,000,
representing 0.01% of the fund&rsquo;s net assets and 9.24% of Vanguard&rsquo;s capitalization. The fund&rsquo;s trustees and officers
are also directors and employees, respectively, of Vanguard.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>C</B>. Various inputs may be used to determine the value
of the fund&rsquo;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs
or methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Level 1</B>&mdash;Quoted prices in active markets for
identical securities.&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Level 2</B>&mdash;Other significant observable inputs
(including quoted prices for similar securities, interest rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Level 3</B>&mdash;Significant unobservable inputs (including
the fund&rsquo;s own assumptions used to determine the fair value of investments). Any investments valued with significant unobservable
inputs are noted on the Statement of Net Assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>Report of Independent Registered
Public Accounting Firm</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">To the Board of Trustees of Vanguard Index Funds and Shareholders
of Vanguard 500 Index Fund</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Opinion on the Financial Statements</B>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">We have audited the accompanying statement of net assets of
Vanguard 500 Index Fund (one of the funds constituting Vanguard Index Funds, referred to hereafter as the &ldquo;Fund&rdquo;) as
of December 31, 2018, the related statement of operations for the year ended December 31, 2018, the statement of changes in net
assets for each of the two years in the period ended December 31, 2018, including the related notes, and the financial highlights
for each of the periods indicated therein (collectively referred to as the &ldquo;financial statements&rdquo;). In our opinion,
the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Fund as of December 31, 2018,
the results of its operations for the year then ended, the changes in its net assets for each of the two years in the period ended
December 31, 2018 and the financial highlights for each of the periods indicated therein in conformity with accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0"><B>Basis for Opinion&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Fund&rsquo;s
management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Fund&rsquo;s financial statements based on our audits. We are a
public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&ldquo;PCAOB&rdquo;) and
are required to be independent with respect to the Fund in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable
rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">We conducted our audits of these financial statements in accordance
with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about
whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks
of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to
those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial
statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as
well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. Our procedures included confirmation of securities owned
as of December 31, 2018 by correspondence with the custodians and brokers and by agreement to the underlying ownership records
of the transfer agent; when replies were not received from brokers, we performed other auditing procedures. We believe that our
audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">/s/PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">Philadelphia, Pennsylvania</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">February 13, 2019</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt/normal Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0">&nbsp;</P>

in The Vanguard Group of Funds since 1975.</P>

fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part owner of the fund. Your fund&rsquo;s
trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides services

meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the sizable personal investments they
have made as private individuals. The independent board members have distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public
service. Each of the trustees and executive officers oversees 212 Vanguard funds.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Important information about access to shareholder reports</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Beginning on January 1, 2021, as permitted by regulations adopted
by the Securities and Exchange Commission, paper copies of your fund&rsquo;s annual and semiannual shareholder reports will no
longer be sent to you by mail, unless you specifically request them. Instead, you will be notified by mail each time a report is
posted on the website and will be provided with a link to access the report.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">If you have already elected to receive shareholder reports electronically,
you will not be affected by this change and do not need to take any action. You may elect to receive shareholder reports and other
communications from the fund electronically by contacting your financial intermediary (such as a broker-dealer or bank) or, if
you invest directly with the fund, by calling Vanguard at one of the phone numbers on the back cover of this report or by logging
on to vanguard.com.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">You may elect to receive paper copies of all future shareholder
reports free of charge. If you invest through a financial intermediary, you can contact the intermediary to request that you continue
to receive paper copies. If you invest directly with the fund, you can call Vanguard at one of the phone numbers on the back cover
of this report or log on to vanguard.com. Your election to receive paper copies will apply to all the funds you hold through an
intermediary or directly with Vanguard.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 18pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>A Note From Our CEO</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><IMG SRC="tv514089-smallcapimg02.jpg" ALT="">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Tim Buckley</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Chairman and Chief Executive Officer</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Dear Shareholder,</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Over the years, I&rsquo;ve found that prudent investors exhibit
a common trait: discipline. No matter how the markets move or what new investing fad hits the headlines, those who stay focused
on their goals and tune out the noise are set up for long-term success.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The prime gateway to investing is saving, and you don&rsquo;t
usually become a saver without a healthy dose of discipline. Savers make the decision to sock away part of their income, which
means spending less and delaying gratification, no matter how difficult that may be.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Of course, disciplined investing extends beyond diligent saving.
The financial markets, in the short term especially, are unpredictable; I have yet to meet the investor who can time them perfectly.
It takes discipline to resist the urge to go all-in when markets are frothy or to retreat when things look bleak.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Staying put with your investments is one strategy for handling
volatility. Another, rebalancing, requires even more discipline because it means steering your money away from strong performers
and toward poorer performers.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Patience&mdash;a form of discipline&mdash;is also the friend
of long-term investors. Higher returns are the potential reward for weathering the market&rsquo;s turbulence and uncertainty.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">It&rsquo;s important to be prepared for that turbulence, whenever
it appears. Don&rsquo;t panic. Don&rsquo;t chase returns or look for answers outside the asset classes you trust. And be sure to
rebalance periodically, even when there&rsquo;s turmoil.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Whether you&rsquo;re a master of self-control, get a boost from
technology, or work with a professional advisor, know that discipline is necessary to get the most out of your investment portfolio.
And know that Vanguard is with you for the entire ride.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Thank you for your continued loyalty.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Sincerely,</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><IMG SRC="tv514089-smallcapimg03.jpg" ALT="">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Mortimer J. Buckley</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Chairman and Chief Executive Officer</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">January 17, 2019</P>

<P STYLE="font: 18pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>Your Fund&rsquo;s Performance
at a Glance</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
the 12 months ended December 31, 2018, returns for Vanguard&rsquo;s three small-capitalization U.S. stock index funds ranged from
about &ndash;6% for Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund to about &ndash;12% for Vanguard Small-Cap Value Index Fund. Vanguard
Small-Cap Index Fund, which contains both growth and value stocks, returned about &ndash;9%. Each fund closely tracked its target
index. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Growth
stocks held up notably better than value stocks, while large-capitalization stocks led mid- and small-caps. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Financial
and industrial stocks detracted most from the Small-Cap Index and Value Index Funds&rsquo; results. Oil and gas stocks and financial
stocks detracted most from the Growth Index Fund&rsquo;s returns. Technology was the top-performing sector for the Small-Cap Index
and Growth Index Funds, while utilities contributed most to the Value Index Fund.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Please
note that in November, Vanguard lowered the investment minimum for the funds&rsquo; Admiral Shares from $10,000 to $3,000.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 18pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>About Your Fund&rsquo;s Expenses</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which
include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating
expenses, which are deducted from a fund&rsquo;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">A fund&rsquo;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its
average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing
costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based
on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The accompanying table illustrates your fund&rsquo;s costs in
two ways:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>Based
on actual fund return.</B> This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &ldquo;Ending
Account Value&rdquo; shown is derived from the fund&rsquo;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would
have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you
invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example,
an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading
&ldquo;Expenses Paid During Period.&rdquo;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>Based
on hypothetical 5% yearly return.</B> This section is intended to help you compare your fund&rsquo;s costs with those of other
mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this
case&mdash;because the return used is not the fund&rsquo;s actual return&mdash;the results do not apply to your investment. The
example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses
based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&rsquo;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples
that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight
and help you compare <I>ongoing</I> costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling
securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus.
If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &ldquo;sales load.&rdquo;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during
the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases
or redemptions.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-right: 0; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: left">You can find more information about the
fund&rsquo;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information
on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&rsquo;s current prospectus.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The calculations are based on expenses incurred in the most recent
six-month period. The funds&rsquo; annualized six-month expense ratios for that period are: for the Small-Cap Index Fund, 0.17%
for Investor Shares, 0.05% for ETF Shares, 0.05% for Admiral Shares, 0.04% for Institutional Shares, and 0.03% for Institutional
Plus Shares; for the Small-Cap Growth Index Fund, 0.19% for Investor Shares, 0.07% for ETF Shares, 0.07% for Admiral Shares, and
0.06% for Institutional Shares; and for the Small-Cap Value Index Fund, 0.19% for Investor Shares, 0.07% for ETF Shares, 0.07%
for Admiral Shares, and 0.06% for Institutional Shares. The dollar amounts shown as &ldquo;Expenses Paid&rdquo; are equal to the
annualized expense ratio multiplied by the average account value over the period, multiplied by the number of days in the most
recent six-month period, then divided by the number of days in the most recent 12-month period (184/365).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Small-Cap Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 18pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 13pt"><B>Notes to Financial Statements</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment
Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers five classes of shares: Investor Shares,
ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares. Each of the share classes has different eligibility
and minimum purchase requirements, and is designed for different types of investors. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE
Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On November 19, 2018, the fund announced changes to the availability
and minimum investment criteria of the Investor and Admiral share classes. It is anticipated that all of the outstanding Investor
Shares will be automatically converted to Admiral Shares beginning in April 2019, with the exception of those held by Vanguard
funds and certain other institutional investors.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>A.</B> The following significant accounting
policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such
policies in preparing its financial statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">1.&nbsp;&nbsp;Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of
the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are
valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades;
such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for
which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the
fund&rsquo;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&rsquo; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board
of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&rsquo;s net asset value.
Temporary cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers
such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">2.&nbsp;&nbsp;Futures Contracts: The fund
uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, maintaining
liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while
maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation
between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid
market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing
broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength
of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse
imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&rsquo;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing
changes in the market value of each contract. Any assets pledged as initial margin for open contracts are noted in the Statement
of Net Assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement
prices. The notional amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the
contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized
appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>


<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 23; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->21<!-- Field: /Sequence --></P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Small-Cap Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During the year ended December 31, 2018,
the fund&rsquo;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively,
based on the average of the notional amounts at each quarter-end during the period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">3. Swap Contracts: The fund has entered into equity swap contracts
to earn the total return on selected reference stocks in the fund&rsquo;s target index. Under the terms of the swaps, the fund
receives the total return on the referenced stock (i.e., receiving the increase or paying the decrease in value of the selected
reference stock and receiving the equivalent of any dividends in respect of the selected referenced stock) over a specified period
of time, applied to a notional amount that represents the value of a designated number of shares of the selected reference stock
at the beginning of the equity swap contract. The fund also pays a floating rate that is based on short-term interest rates, applied
to the notional amount. At the same time, the fund generally invests an amount approximating the notional amount of the swap in
high-quality temporary cash investments.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The notional amounts of swap contracts are not recorded in the
Statement of Net Assets. Swaps are valued daily based on market quotations received from independent pricing services or recognized
dealers and the change in value is recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations
as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until termination of the swap, at which time realized gain (loss) is recorded.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">A risk associated with all types of swaps is the possibility
that a counterparty may default on its obligation to pay net amounts due to the fund. The fund&rsquo;s maximum amount subject to
counterparty risk is the unrealized appreciation on the swap contract. The fund mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into
swaps only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, entering into master netting
arrangements with its counterparties, and requiring its counterparties to transfer collateral as security for their performance.
In the absence of a default, the collateral pledged or received by the fund cannot be repledged, resold, or rehypothecated. In
the event of a counterparty&rsquo;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any swap contracts with that counterparty,
determine the net amount owed by either party in accordance with its master netting arrangements, and sell or retain any collateral
held up to the net amount owed to the fund under the master netting arrangements. The swap contracts contain provisions whereby
a counterparty may terminate open contracts if the fund net assets decline below a certain level, triggering a payment by the
fund if the fund is in a net liability position at the time of the termination. The payment amount would be reduced by any collateral
the fund has pledged. Any securities pledged as collateral for open contracts are noted in the Statement of Net Assets. The value
of collateral received or pledged is compared daily to the value of the swap contracts exposure with each counterparty, and any
difference, if in excess of a specified minimum transfer amount, is adjusted and settled within two business days.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During the year ended December 31, 2018, the fund&rsquo;s average
amounts of investments in total return swaps represented less than 1% of net assets, based on the average of notional amounts at
each quarter-end during the period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">4. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify
as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&rsquo;s tax positions
taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2015&ndash;2018), and has concluded that no provision for federal income
tax is required in the fund&rsquo;s financial statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Small-Cap Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">5. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded
on the ex-dividend date. Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital
gains for financial reporting purposes.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">6. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends
its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time, and are
required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market
fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this
occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled before the opening of the market on the next business day. The fund further mitigates
its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties,
monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master
securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&rsquo;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may
terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed
to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the event
of a default, the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received
in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during
the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested
cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan. During the term of the loan, the fund is entitled to all distributions
made on or in respect of the loaned securities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">7. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed
by The Vanguard Group (&ldquo;Vanguard&rdquo;) participate in a $3.1 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate
of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if
any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&rsquo;s
regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment
fee of 0.10% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&rsquo;s
board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&rsquo;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings
under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon the higher of the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate, federal funds
effective rate, or overnight bank funding rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2018,
or at any time during the period then ended.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">8. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date.
Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts
on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities.
Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses)
on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Small-Cap Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings,
except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included
in Management and Administrative expenses), and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each
class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses
on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>B.</B> In accordance with the terms of a Funds&rsquo; Service
Agreement (the &ldquo;FSA&rdquo;) between Vanguard and the fund, Vanguard furnishes to the fund investment advisory, corporate
management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services at Vanguard&rsquo;s cost of operations (as defined by the FSA).
These costs of operations are allocated to the fund based on methods and guidelines approved by the board of trustees. Vanguard
does not require reimbursement in the current period for certain costs of operations (such as deferred compensation/benefits and
risk/insurance costs); the fund&rsquo;s liability for these costs of operations is included in Payables to Vanguard on the Statement
of Net Assets. All other costs of operations payable to Vanguard are generally settled twice a month.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Upon the request of Vanguard, the fund may invest up to 0.40%
of its net assets as capital in Vanguard. At December 31, 2018, the fund had contributed to Vanguard capital in the amount of $4,571,000,
representing 0.01% of the fund&rsquo;s net assets and 1.83% of Vanguard&rsquo;s capitalization. The fund&rsquo;s trustees and officers
are also directors and employees, respectively, of Vanguard.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>C.</B> Various inputs may be used to determine the value of
the fund&rsquo;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs or
methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Level 1</B>&mdash;Quoted prices in active markets for identical
securities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Level 2</B>&mdash;Other significant observable inputs (including
quoted prices for similar securities, interest rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Level 3</B>&mdash;Significant unobservable inputs (including
the fund&rsquo;s own assumptions used to determine the fair value of investments). Any investments valued with significant unobservable
inputs are noted on the Statement of Net Assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Small-Cap Growth Index Fund</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 13pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>Notes to Financial Statements</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes
of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Shares. Each of the share classes has different eligibility
and minimum purchase requirements, and is designed for different types of investors. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE
Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On November 19, 2018, the fund announced changes to the availability
and minimum investment criteria of the Investor and Admiral share classes. It is anticipated that all of the outstanding Investor
Shares will be automatically converted to Admiral Shares beginning in April 2019, with the exception of those held by Vanguard
funds and certain other institutional investors.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>A. </B>The following significant accounting
policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such
policies in preparing its financial statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close
of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued
at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which
market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&rsquo;s
pricing time but after the close of the securities&rsquo; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees
to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&rsquo;s net asset value. Temporary
cash investments are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors
as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index
futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, maintaining liquidity,
and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or
sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining
a cash balance for liquidity. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between
changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.
Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing
broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength
of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse
imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&rsquo;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing
changes in the market value of each contract. Any assets pledged as initial margin for open contracts are noted in the Statement
of Net Assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement
prices. The notional amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the
contracts are recorded in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as
unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>


<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 43; Value: 1 -->
